2017 meeting minutes documented a motion approved to disburse a sum from the earnings of the Worthy Poor Fund to a resident, with a planned six-month follow-up to determine ability to repay that the chair says never happened.

budget_items.topic: Statutory investment limits on trust funds
budget_items.what_was_said: State law caps the share of trust funds that can be invested in bank or insurance company stocks once the trust exceeds a stated total value, and caps the share in any single bank or insurance company's stock.
The chair noted the state's municipal depository trust pool, which the town does not use, was recently paying a stated daily rate.

decisions.decision: Chair will continue investigating whether the town is liable to repay Worthy Poor Fund money over unresolved 2008/2017 loan follow-ups and will inform the executive (town manager) of findings.
Board will pursue Attorney General PCIF (cy pres) filings to modify declarations for the American Legion Fund, the Gazebo Fund, and the Sidewalk Fund, whose original stated purposes no longer exist.
Board will continue using the private trust company (Bartholomew and Company) to manage investments rather than having the treasurer take that role.
Chair will do a clean study review of the draft operating/investment policy with Richard before bringing it to a formal vote; no vote taken tonight.
Richard will identify a date between November 13 and the end of the month for an additional meeting, to be posted at the November 13 meeting.

minutes.summary: The Trust Fund Commission spent most of the meeting on the chair's legal review of municipal gift and trust law, including a disclosure that 2008 and 2017 disbursements from the Worthy Poor Fund were never followed up on for repayment, raising a question of town liability. The board also walked through a draft investment/operating policy line by line without voting on it, and ratified minutes from two prior meetings before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The chair's legal review found 2008 and 2017 payments from the Worthy Poor Fund were never followed up on for repayment, raising a possible town liability.
The board decided to pursue state filings to update the stated purposes of the American Legion, Gazebo, and Sidewalk funds, which no longer apply.
The board reviewed a draft investment and operating policy line by line but took no vote, planning a final review before adoption.
The board opted to keep the outside trust company managing fund investments rather than shifting that role to the treasurer.

why_it_matters: A finding that the town owes money back to a poor-relief fund would touch town finances and could require repayment or a legal opinion before it is resolved.
Updating the purpose of the American Legion, Gazebo, and Sidewalk funds through the state process changes what that money can legally be spent on going forward.
The investment and operating policy under review will set the rules for how the town's trust funds are managed once it is finalized and voted on.
